facts.label: Period scope conflict
facts.text: The run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as the current period and fiscal 2025 as the prior period, but the sources include the annual report for the year ended July 31, 2026, signed September 22, 2026, which is later than the quarter ended April 30, 2026. The label could also mean the calendar quarter ended September 30, 2026, which no source covers. Showing the April 2026 quarter as current leaves out the later year-end balance sheet, and showing the annual report as current departs from the run setting

facts.text: Debt reduction, not earnings, has kept total debt over EBITDA near 1.5x to 1.6x. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 1,133,915 thousand at July 31, 2024 to USD 922,979 thousand a year later and USD 867,959 thousand at July 31, 2026, as term-loan repayments of USD 205,000 thousand and USD 56,264 thousand were made in fiscal 2025 and 2026, while reported EBITDA fell from USD 714,655 thousand to USD 615,839 thousand and USD 541,912 thousand. The ratio therefore moved only from 1.59x to 1.50x and 1.60x. Repayments slowed sharply in fiscal 2026 while EBITDA kept falling, so another earnings decline without a further paydown would lift leverage; net debt over EBITDA already rose from 0.55x to 0.71x as cash fell and EBITDA declined. Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96

facts.label: Analysis by dimension
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate against the debt schedule. Cash plus the issuer-stated unused availability under the asset-based facility was USD 1,296,988 thousand at July 31, 2026 and USD 1,240,176 thousand at January 31, 2026, the lowest cash of the dates shown, when cash was USD 242,176 thousand. Maturities are small until the senior unsecured notes due 2029 (USD 502,814 thousand in fiscal 2030 including other debt) and the term loan due November 15, 2030 (USD 356,219 thousand in fiscal 2031). The facility that supplies the availability expires on November 15, 2028, before either, and its availability follows a borrowing base, with letters of credit outstanding not stated. Its only maintenance test is a springing fixed-charge coverage covenant of 1.0x that applies only when adjusted excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base availability or the commitment and USD 60,000 thousand; the issuer states no reported ratio or headroom, so none is worked out here. Outside debt, standby repurchase obligations on dealer floor-plan financing were USD 3,315,731 thousand at July 31, 2026, of which USD 1,981,105 thousand expires within a year; they are contingent and not in total debt. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-01-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C32; calculation C30

facts.text: Scale and diversification support the business risk, but the earnings base is cyclical and weakening in North America. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the benign view is cash use. In fiscal 2026 payouts exceeded operating cash flow after capital spending by USD 55,055 thousand, cash fell by USD 104,608 thousand, and USD 264,174 thousand of repurchase authority remains while North American towable earnings are falling. If repurchases continued at that pace with operating cash flow near USD 321,223 thousand, the debt reduction that supports creditors would stall, and the unquantified dividend conditions could begin to bind. Against that, management itself lists reducing or ceasing dividends among its responses to a cash shortfall, so payouts are a lever, not a commitment. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business profile is adequate: scale and a three-way split across North American towables, North American motorized and Europe cushion any single market, but demand is discretionary and cyclical, so revenue is durable in level and weak in direction. Thor is the largest recreational vehicle maker in North America by units and revenue, with about 36.8% of towable retail registrations and 49.8% of motorhome registrations, and fiscal 2026 net sales were flat at +0.3% although North American towable sales fell 16.1%, because European sales rose 9.0% and motorized sales 12.8%. The order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand is 8.0% higher, but the gain sits in towables at +74.6% while motorized is 27.5% lower, so visibility is uneven. Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.text: Earnings are the weakest dimension: reported EBITDA has fallen three years running, by 18.21%, 13.83% and 12.00%, to USD 541,912 thousand in fiscal 2026, which is 37.98% below fiscal 2023, while net sales are only 4.33% below fiscal 2024. EBITDA margin has compressed from 7.12% to 5.64% as fixed-cost absorption, product mix and tariff-related material costs bite, and the fiscal fourth quarter was 42.17% below a year earlier, so the run-rate entering fiscal 2027 is lower than the year's total suggests. facts.text: The strongest evidence against comfort in the level of credit quality is the trend. Fiscal fourth-quarter EBITDA was 42.17% below the prior year on net sales 8.41% lower, and four times that quarter, USD 520,016 thousand, would already put total debt at 1.67x EBITDA. North American motorized backlog fell 27.5%, and management expects the rest of calendar 2026 and possibly beyond to stay under pressure from interest rates, tariffs and fuel prices linked to disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, so a further decline is plausible rather than remote. facts.label: Company and group structure
facts.text: Thor is a listed manufacturer with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so the creditor question is financial policy rather than owner behaviour. It states that it is the sole owner of its operating subsidiaries, which sit in three groups: North American towables and motorized brands, the Erwin Hymer Group in Europe, and the Airxcel and Postle supply businesses, and on July 1, 2026 it took full control of the Roadpass Digital holding company, now under Airxcel. The notes carry guarantees from subsidiaries that are not named in the supplied text, and more than half of cash is held in Europe, so whether the parent and the guarantors can reach the cash and earnings of the European group is not established. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is transactional, discretionary and cyclical rather than recurring: vehicles are built to dealer order, sold to independent dealers who finance inventory with floor-plan lenders, and volume follows consumer confidence and interest rates. In fiscal 2026 shipments fell 11.8% in total and 20.7% in North American towables, while price and mix added 4.6% per unit in towables, so net sales held up through motorized volume, mix and the euro rather than towable demand. Visibility comes from the order backlog, which equals 34.33% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and from one dealer at 13.0% of sales whose bargaining power rises as dealers consolidate. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are defended only partly under volume pressure. Material, labour, freight and warranty costs are the main costs, and in North American towables cost of sales rose to 88.8% of net sales from 86.9% as overhead absorption worsened with lower volume, which is why pre-tax income fell 2.51 times as fast as net sales. North American capacity can be cut quickly, but European reductions need works council agreements and bring negotiated separation costs, and restructuring charges rose to USD 58,889 thousand in fiscal 2026 across all segments. Selling, general and administrative expense eased 2.1% mainly through lower incentive pay, a cushion that shrinks as profit falls. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense and entry is easy: about 80 manufacturers compete in the United States and Canada, the principal rivals are Forest River and Winnebago Industries, and the industry has low barriers to entry, so share and price are contested and pricing power is limited. Buyer power is high because one consolidating dealer is 13.0% of sales and two floor-plan lenders decide how much inventory dealers can carry, which can cut orders quickly. Supplier power is concentrated in chassis, where a limited number of suppliers allocate supply in shortages and chassis cannot easily be substituted, and substitutes include used vehicles and other leisure spending, which gain in downturns. Each force acts on volume and margin, not on solvency, and Thor's scale and low leverage let it absorb more of that pressure than a smaller maker. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Macro and policy factors do alter credit quality here. Tariffs raised component costs that were not fully passed on, a court ruling opened a refund process for tariffs paid under one authority, and a temporary global tariff expired in late July 2026, so net tariff cost is uncertain and refunds could help cash. Interest rates and consumer confidence drive retail demand and dealer carrying costs, fuel prices linked to the Iran conflict may hurt retail demand, emissions rules reach Thor through chassis makers, and new European limits on formaldehyde emissions phase in from calendar 2026 and 2027, which can raise product cost. Currency matters because about 34% of sales are in euros and other currencies and the euro term loan is an economic hedge. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is another leg down in North American towable retail demand from high borrowing costs, tariffs and fuel prices, with dealers destocking faster than retail, as in fiscal 2026 when company wholesale units fell 20.5% against retail registrations down 18.5%. The first operational break is operating deleverage in towables, where pre-tax income fell 2.51 times as fast as net sales, and the second is a European margin squeeze. If EBITDA repeated the 37.98% fall of fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026 from its fiscal 2026 level it would be USD 336,110 thousand, EBITDA margin 3.50%, total debt 2.58x EBITDA and EBITDA 7.70x cash interest; the milder run-rate case of four times the fourth quarter gives USD 520,016 thousand and 1.67x. With capital spending, interest and working capital unchanged and the effective tax rate at 26.8%, free cash flow in the stress case falls to about USD 18,189 thousand, so payouts at the fiscal 2026 level would draw about USD 205,702 thousand of cash and leave about USD 276,286 thousand, while the facility, undrawn at year end, still adds availability subject to its borrowing base, which shrinks with receivables and inventory. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: Management levers are cutting repurchases and dividends, which management lists as responses to a shortfall, reducing capital spending, lowering incentive pay and extending restructuring, and these are enough to avoid a liquidity event in the case shown. The credit event that the levers do not address is a dealer default that triggers repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand gross, which is 2.56x liquidity before resale value, and the springing fixed-charge covenant of the facility applies only if excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base or facility size and USD 60,000 thousand. Default is not the base case: nothing in the evidence points to one, and liquidity would remain positive in the stress case. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Thor presents an adequate business profile supported by North American market leadership, a three-way segment split and a low-leverage balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by three years of falling earnings, payouts above free cash flow and contingent dealer obligations. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but weakening, because free cash flow converted only 31.16% of EBITDA. Reported leverage of 1.60x is low in absolute terms, and no peer set or ratings are supplied for comparison with other leveraged issuers. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilising before the facility expires in November 2028 and the notes fall due in October 2029, with the term loan following in November 2030. The primary downside path is a further fall in North American towable demand that deepens operating deleverage while payouts continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreements, the indenture, the proxy statement, covenant certificates, unit-level goodwill headroom and dealer-level repurchase exposure. Top risk: earnings erosion in North American towables combined with payouts above free cash flow. spans.text: # Financial foundation for Thor Industries Inc (tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Financial foundation for Thor Industries Inc (issuer tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the audited annual statements for fiscal 2023 to 2026 and the unaudited interim statements to April 30, 2026 in the four filings supplied, in US dollars.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025 | 2025-09-24 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 27b5c630a527a6271b1f13f1fc3ef0e98de65299bd284130796093caf8ee41b8 | Fiscal 2023 income statement and depreciation, July 31, 2024 balance sheet, fiscal 2025 and 2024 statements as first reported, debt note, backlog and dealer inventory |

| 10-Q_2026-01-31_tho.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended January 31, 2026 | 2026-03-03 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 2d5dd6d4d39ec96796c1234b9270746db0bc632c4f50e97949822179bc2e0a7c | January 31, 2026 cash and unused asset-based facility availability |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 | 669c49faf30b43f4c90d50803e2762c33d2a05a15661936429656f70fc9ae64a | Source gaps, the period-scope conflict, the reclassified cash-flow comparatives and the unexplained short-term financial obligations line |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage is low at 1.60x total debt and 0.71x net debt to EBITDA at July 31, 2026, but EBITDA fell for a third year and the fiscal fourth quarter was 42.17% below a year earlier, so creditors rely on a shrinking earnings base.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C12; calculation C19; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23

Liquidity cushions the decline: the asset-based facility had about USD 815 million available at year-end, the first sizeable maturity is the USD 500 million 2029 notes, and cash fell 17.83% over the year while dividends and buybacks exceeded free cash flow. EBITDA is built from reported lines because the issuer prints none, and USD 60,839 thousand of short-term financial obligations sit outside debt; counting them lifts total debt to 1.71x EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation C36; calculation C28; calculation C27; calculation C33; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 93
### Analysis by dimension

Debt reduction, not earnings, has kept total debt over EBITDA near 1.5x to 1.6x. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 1,133,915 thousand at July 31, 2024 to USD 922,979 thousand a year later and USD 867,959 thousand at July 31, 2026, as term-loan repayments of USD 205,000 thousand and USD 56,264 thousand were made in fiscal 2025 and 2026, while reported EBITDA fell from USD 714,655 thousand to USD 615,839 thousand and USD 541,912 thousand. The ratio therefore moved only from 1.59x to 1.50x and 1.60x. Repayments slowed sharply in fiscal 2026 while EBITDA kept falling, so another earnings decline without a further paydown would lift leverage; net debt over EBITDA already rose from 0.55x to 0.71x as cash fell and EBITDA declined.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96

Coverage improved from 8.27x to 10.50x and 12.42x of EBITDA over cash interest, but the gain came from the liability side: cash interest paid fell from USD 86,421 thousand to USD 58,626 thousand and USD 43,633 thousand as the term loan was repaid and repriced, while EBITDA fell. The senior unsecured notes due 2029 pay a fixed coupon and the term loan floats on SOFR and EURIBOR, so cover is sensitive to base rates on the floating term loan and to earnings throughout.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; calculation C12

Cash-flow quality weakened in fiscal 2026. Operating cash flow fell from USD 577,923 thousand to USD 321,223 thousand, with inventories absorbing USD 73,282 thousand, and free cash flow after purchases of property, plant and equipment was USD 168,836 thousand against USD 454,936 thousand. Dividends and share repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand exceeded it, so cash fell, even with USD 67,875 thousand of asset-sale proceeds in investing flows; free cash flow was 31.16% of EBITDA against 73.87% a year earlier.
Basis: calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96

Liquidity is adequate against the debt schedule. Cash plus the issuer-stated unused availability under the asset-based facility was USD 1,296,988 thousand at July 31, 2026 and USD 1,240,176 thousand at January 31, 2026, the lowest cash of the dates shown, when cash was USD 242,176 thousand. Maturities are small until the senior unsecured notes due 2029 (USD 502,814 thousand in fiscal 2030 including other debt) and the term loan due November 15, 2030 (USD 356,219 thousand in fiscal 2031). The facility that supplies the availability expires on November 15, 2028, before either, and its availability follows a borrowing base, with letters of credit outstanding not stated. Its only maintenance test is a springing fixed-charge coverage covenant of 1.0x that applies only when adjusted excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base availability or the commitment and USD 60,000 thousand; the issuer states no reported ratio or headroom, so none is worked out here. Outside debt, standby repurchase obligations on dealer floor-plan financing were USD 3,315,731 thousand at July 31, 2026, of which USD 1,981,105 thousand expires within a year; they are contingent and not in total debt.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-01-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 50; calculation C32; calculation C30

Definition and data-quality risk sits in the earnings measure. Reported EBITDA is calculated and keeps other income, net; the cash flow statement shows fiscal 2026 gains of USD 36,696 thousand on disposals and USD 22,235 thousand on investments, and without those total debt over EBITDA would be 1.80x (Analyst Judgement, not applied to the ratios). Short-term financial obligations of USD 60,839 thousand are excluded from debt because no note describes them. The twelve months to April 30, 2026 show EBITDA of USD 636,712 thousand, but the fourth quarter that followed produced USD 130,004 thousand against USD 224,804 thousand a year earlier, so the April ratios are stale.
Basis: calculation C34; calculation C33; calculation C15; calculation C18; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 95

The March 2024 hail event is one economic event with three figures: property losses and expenses of USD 69,822 thousand, insurance proceeds of USD 81,975 thousand net of the deductible and a fiscal 2025 gain of USD 12,153 thousand, of which USD 5,837 thousand is business interruption; the gain sits in other income, net and therefore in fiscal 2025 reported EBITDA. On non-debt funding, accounts payable rose by USD 90,409 thousand in fiscal 2025, which management attributes to extended vendor payment terms on certain raw material purchases, and were then flat in fiscal 2026; no supplier-finance program and no defined-benefit pension or retiree medical obligation was found by search. The only dated event after the year-end is the September 10, 2026 announcement of a unified North American operating group, which changes no fiscal 2026 figure and states no debt or cash effect, so it is excluded from period figures.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 131; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 132

## Gaps

- Reported EBITDA is calculated in every period because none of the four filings prints EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or covenant EBITDA; this restricts leverage and coverage to a reported, unadjusted basis and leaves covenant EBITDA unknown. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain earnings releases or the compliance definition in the credit agreement.

- Other income, net sits inside reported EBITDA and includes gains on disposals and unrealized investment gains that the cash flow statement quantifies only in part (USD 58,931 thousand in fiscal 2026); the rest of the line is not quantified, which restricts the underlying earnings run rate. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the breakdown of other income, net.

- Short-term financial obligations of USD 60,839 thousand at July 31, 2026 and USD 60,112 thousand a year earlier have no explanatory note, so whether they are debt-like is not established and they are excluded from total debt; this restricts total debt, net debt and every leverage ratio. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the issuer description of the line.

- The debt stack is not drawn: the filings do not state which of the term loan and the asset-based facility are secured, how they rank against the senior unsecured notes or who guarantees them, and the credit agreements and indenture are not supplied; this restricts any statement of structural priority and cumulative leverage. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed agreements, the indenture and the subsidiary list.
- Debt by seniority is not disclosed beyond the senior unsecured notes, so senior secured and subordinated debt are not supplied in any period. Severity: Medium. Action: as for the debt stack.

- The amount of letters of credit outstanding under the asset-based facility is not stated, and unused availability is the issuer approximation under a borrowing base; this restricts the undrawn figure in the liquidity table. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the borrowing base certificate.

- Unused asset-based facility availability at July 31, 2024 is not stated in the supplied filings, so the undrawn figure and the liquidity ratio for fiscal 2024 are not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the fiscal 2024 annual report.

- The statements print dashes or omit lines that other periods carry: asset impairment charges for fiscal 2024, borrowings on term-loan facilities for fiscal 2025 and 2026, payments of debt issuance costs for fiscal 2025 and 2026, revolving facility borrowings and repayments for fiscal 2025, business acquisitions for fiscal 2025 and nine months 2025, and several lines the nine-month statements do not print; none is treated as zero. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the credit metrics.

- Fiscal 2025 and 2024 cash-flow lines were reclassified in the fiscal 2026 report, while the nine-month columns follow the quarterly report classification, so line-level comparisons across those columns are not like for like even though operating cash flow is unchanged. Severity: Low. Action: use the fiscal 2026 classification for the annual columns.

- No fourth-quarter figures are reported and no balance sheet at October 31, 2025 is supplied, so quarterly series are calculated by subtraction and labelled calculated. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the quarterly report for the quarter ended October 31, 2025 if that balance sheet is needed.

- The twelve months to April 30, 2026 are shown because the run settings name the third quarter of 2026 as current, but the fiscal 2026 annual report is later; interim ratios are stale against fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter EBITDA 42.17% lower than a year earlier. Severity: Medium. Action: the run owner confirms the current period.

- Lease liabilities are not on their own balance-sheet lines; operating lease payments of USD 52,220 thousand undiscounted and finance lease payments of USD 940 thousand are in the contractual obligations table, so they are outside total debt and not stated at present value. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the headline ratios.

- The Euro term loan is printed in US dollars only, so its Euro principal and the exchange rate are not established; total Euro-denominated debt of USD 325,768 thousand moves with the exchange rate and is reconciled to the Euro term loan, the Euro unsecured note and other debt. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the term loan agreement or the Euro balance.

- Interest income and exceptional items are not presented as separate income statement lines; interest is shown net, and impairments, gains and insurance settlements appear in the cash flow statement and in other income, net. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the headline ratios.

- Segment structure may change from fiscal 2027 after the September 10, 2026 announcement; fiscal 2026 segment data follow the three reportable segments in the annual report. Severity: Low. Action: label segment figures as the fiscal 2026 structure.
- Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, so only total purchases of property, plant and equipment are carried. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for the headline ratios.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Thor is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified in the filings supplied, so creditors face the RV cycle and shareholder payouts rather than sponsor extraction, though ownership and board detail sits in a proxy statement not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 86

Payouts are the main governance signal: dividends and share repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand in fiscal 2026 were 132.61% of operating cash flow after capital spending, against 34.90% a year earlier, while the quarterly dividend was still raised to $0.52. Dealer concentration is the main business risk, with one dealer at 13.0% of net sales and standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand on dealer inventory financing.

### Key findings

No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes the extraction and exit-pressure risks of a sponsor-owned credit, but the evidence is the annual report's silence rather than a disclosure of holders. The common stock trades on the New York Stock Exchange, the annual report counts only a small number of holders of record, and ownership, directors and related-party dealings are incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a holder of 10% or more cannot be ruled out. Certain business combinations that 75% of the directors have not approved need the vote of 75% of the shares, which slows any change of control.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 86

Scale and diversification support the business risk, but the earnings base is cyclical and weakening in North America. Thor is the largest recreational vehicle maker in North America by units and revenue, and fiscal 2026 net sales split 33.1% North American towable, 25.6% North American motorized and 34.3% European, with a supply business at 10.2% before eliminations. North American towable net sales fell 16.1% and its pre-tax income fell 40.4%, while Europe grew 9.0%, or 3.1% at constant currency, and North American motorized 12.8%, so group net sales rose only 0.3% and pre-tax income fell 19.4% as gross margin narrowed from 14.0% to 12.6%.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 66

Dealer concentration and repurchase obligations are the largest structural exposure outside debt. One dealer, FreedomRoads, accounted for 13.0% of net sales in fiscal 2026 and 14.0% a year earlier, and for 13.0% of trade receivables, while standby repurchase obligations on dealer inventory financing were USD 3,315,731 thousand, 3.79x total contractual debt principal, and two floor-plan lenders held about 50% of the floored dollars for Thor products. Losses on settled repurchases were not material in fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2025 and USD 7,107 thousand in fiscal 2024, so the obligation is contingent, but a floor-plan default by a large dealer in a downturn would become a cash call that the filings do not size by dealer.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; calculation A07

Financial policy is shareholder-oriented but has so far been funded without adding debt. The dividend rose to $0.52 a quarter in October 2025, repurchases rose to USD 115,126 thousand in fiscal 2026 from USD 52,647 thousand, and USD 264,174 thousand of the USD 400,000 thousand authorization remains until July 31, 2027, yet term-loan repayments of USD 205,000 thousand in fiscal 2025 and USD 56,264 thousand in fiscal 2026 reduced debt. Dividends are conditioned on a minimum level of adjusted excess cash availability and a fixed charge coverage test, which the filings do not quantify.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 128; calculation A09

Fiscal 2026 was the first of the three years shown in which payouts exceeded free cash flow. Dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand compared with USD 168,836 thousand of operating cash flow after capital spending, 132.61% against 34.90% in fiscal 2025 and 42.01% in fiscal 2024, so cash fell by USD 104,608 thousand as operating cash flow dropped to USD 321,223 thousand from USD 577,923 thousand. Of the USD 481,988 thousand of cash at year end, USD 263,889 thousand or 54.75% sat in Europe, so cash within easy reach of the United States parent is smaller than the headline.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A04; calculation A14

Acquisition behaviour is small and not debt-funded, but goodwill is large relative to equity. Business acquisitions cost USD 9,555 thousand net of cash in fiscal 2026, nothing in fiscal 2025 and USD 7,314 thousand in fiscal 2024, and the July 1, 2026 step to full ownership of the Roadpass Digital holding company carried USD 93,987 thousand of net fair value including the previously held interest, with immaterial consideration. Goodwill of USD 1,916,330 thousand plus amortizable intangibles of USD 684,494 thousand is 37.39% of total assets and 61.05% of equity, and about 80% of the goodwill sits in reporting units whose fair value exceeds carrying value by less than 25%, with the valuation of the USD 464 million allocated to Airxcel a critical audit matter. A modest fall in forecasts could therefore force an impairment that reduces equity and earnings without a cash cost, although whether any covenant definition adds back impairments is not established.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation A05; calculation A08; calculation A13

Restructuring is widening and the group is being reorganised, which should improve cost control but weakens period comparability. Restructuring charges rose to USD 58,889 thousand in fiscal 2026 from USD 42,123 thousand across North American towable, motorized, Europe and corporate, and gains on fixed asset sales of USD 36,942 thousand in North American towable partly offset them. On September 10, 2026 Thor announced a unified North American operation and three operating groups, and its reportable segments may change from fiscal 2027.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 132; calculation A06

Disclosure of financial results is strong but disclosure of creditor terms is thin, so the sponsor and governance risk level is medium, not low. The financial statements and internal control over financial reporting carry unqualified audit opinions, yet the credit agreements, the indenture with its guarantor list, the subsidiary list and the proxy statement are not supplied, so legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and liens, guarantor coverage and related-party dealings cannot be assessed. Medium reflects documented payouts above free cash flow in one year and missing capacity evidence, set against no documented extraction, no described liability management and steady debt reduction.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, pages 87–89
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the benign view is cash use. In fiscal 2026 payouts exceeded operating cash flow after capital spending by USD 55,055 thousand, cash fell by USD 104,608 thousand, and USD 264,174 thousand of repurchase authority remains while North American towable earnings are falling. If repurchases continued at that pace with operating cash flow near USD 321,223 thousand, the debt reduction that supports creditors would stall, and the unquantified dividend conditions could begin to bind. Against that, management itself lists reducing or ceasing dividends among its responses to a cash shortfall, so payouts are a lever, not a commitment.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 128; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A04

A proxy statement showing a holder of 10% or more, or a controlling group, would change the ownership conclusion, and executed credit agreements with wide restricted-payment or investment baskets, or a guarantor group narrower than the operating group, would raise the risk level. Payouts held below free cash flow in fiscal 2027 while the order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand converts to sales would lower it, as would continued term-loan repayment; a repurchase claim from a floor-plan lender would raise it.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118

- Legal capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and liens is not assessed because the credit agreements and the indenture are not supplied, so the issuer's summary of payment conditions is the only evidence and actual capacity could be wider or narrower than the payout record implies.

- The behaviour record covers three fiscal years, so the conclusion that financial policy is creditor-compatible is not tested through a full downturn in which payouts, dealer defaults and repurchase obligations would interact.

- The business acquired in fiscal 2026 for USD 9,555 thousand is not named and no pro forma earnings are given, so the conclusion that acquisition appetite is small rests on cash paid, not on purchase multiples or integration evidence.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Thor has no sponsor buyout, recapitalisation or acquisition financing in the evidence: it is a listed company and the four filings state no purchase price, entry multiple, equity contribution or sources and uses to report.

Its senior debt was last raised on October 14, 2021, when it issued USD 500,000 thousand of senior unsecured notes due October 15, 2029 and used the proceeds with cash to repay USD 500,000 thousand drawn on the asset-based facility. The notes rank equally with other senior debt and behind secured debt, and the guarantors named in the indenture are not identified in the supplied text. spans.text: # Fundamental credit for Thor Industries Inc (tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit for Thor Industries Inc (issuer tho-730263), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated fundamental credit view built from the four pinned filings and the three supplied module outputs, in US dollars. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2025 | 2025-09-24 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 27b5c630a527a6271b1f13f1fc3ef0e98de65299bd284130796093caf8ee41b8 | Fiscal 2025 comparatives for earnings, debt amendments and market share |

| 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026 | 2026-09-22 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 316d37acfd5355f95d77a4fcd20f159e1820ab83d824307ddefc9ea9fac9d427 | Controlling source for the business, industry outlook, segments, debt note, liquidity, cash flows, dealer financing, impairment testing, restructuring and the subsequent event |

| 10-Q_2026-01-31_tho.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended January 31, 2026 | 2026-03-03 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 2d5dd6d4d39ec96796c1234b9270746db0bc632c4f50e97949822179bc2e0a7c | Cash and availability at January 31, 2026, the seasonal low point |

| 10-Q_2026-04-30_tho.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarterly period ended April 30, 2026 | 2026-06-03 (date signed; filing date not stated) | 9ee9df385c64fefe869e7564f17e68909059705fb227fdc216bfb5680263494d | Interim position at April 30, 2026 and nine-month trends |
| Supplied handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness (CP-0) | CP-0 | 669c49faf30b43f4c90d50803e2762c33d2a05a15661936429656f70fc9ae64a | Missing documents, the period label conflict and the earnings definition gap |

| Financial foundation (CP-1) | CP-1 | 6271cc4078683b4cf11188f8bd4645e7eaabe470cda94f2f2808abf1c1356d1a | EBITDA, leverage, coverage, free cash flow, liquidity, maturity ladder and debt reconciliation |

| Business & governance (CP-1A) | CP-1A | 80a9ce0d2cfc61c627a7a0f517a591d1703f7f2db373bda2c1f934205eb66b8c | Ownership, governance, dealer exposure, goodwill headroom, capital allocation and the sponsor and governance risk level |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Thor's low leverage, large liquidity and distant maturities protect creditors through another weak year, but earnings have fallen three years running and payouts now exceed free cash flow, so the trend, not the level, is the risk to watch.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Reported EBITDA fell 12.00% to USD 541,912 thousand in fiscal 2026, lifting total debt to EBITDA from 1.50x to 1.60x, yet cash plus unused facility availability of USD 1,296,988 thousand is 5.79x one year of payouts and 98.09% of debt principal falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031. Cash use is the swing factor: dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand exceeded free cash flow of USD 168,836 thousand.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K01; calculation K02; calculation K06; calculation K09; calculation K10; calculation K11
### Key findings

The business profile is adequate: scale and a three-way split across North American towables, North American motorized and Europe cushion any single market, but demand is discretionary and cyclical, so revenue is durable in level and weak in direction. Thor is the largest recreational vehicle maker in North America by units and revenue, with about 36.8% of towable retail registrations and 49.8% of motorhome registrations, and fiscal 2026 net sales were flat at +0.3% although North American towable sales fell 16.1%, because European sales rose 9.0% and motorized sales 12.8%. The order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand is 8.0% higher, but the gain sits in towables at +74.6% while motorized is 27.5% lower, so visibility is uneven.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Earnings are the weakest dimension: reported EBITDA has fallen three years running, by 18.21%, 13.83% and 12.00%, to USD 541,912 thousand in fiscal 2026, which is 37.98% below fiscal 2023, while net sales are only 4.33% below fiscal 2024. EBITDA margin has compressed from 7.12% to 5.64% as fixed-cost absorption, product mix and tariff-related material costs bite, and the fiscal fourth quarter was 42.17% below a year earlier, so the run-rate entering fiscal 2027 is lower than the year's total suggests.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation K01; calculation K02; calculation K03; calculation K04; calculation K05

Leverage is low and is the main support: total debt is 1.60x reported EBITDA and net debt 0.71x, and EBITDA covers cash interest 12.42x because debt was repaid and the term loan repriced. The ratio is rising, from 1.50x a year earlier, because EBITDA fell faster than debt, and EBITDA here is calculated from reported lines and includes gains on asset sales and investments; without those gains total debt would be 1.80x, which is the analyst's adjustment and not an issuer figure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K06; calculation K07; calculation K08

Liquidity and the maturity profile give a wide buffer: cash of USD 481,988 thousand plus about USD 815,000 thousand of unused asset-based facility availability is USD 1,296,988 thousand, and 98.09% of debt principal falls due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031. Two limits apply: the facility expires on November 15, 2028, before the notes and the term loan, and its availability follows a borrowing base, and 54.75% of cash sits in Europe, where repatriation to the United States parent may carry withholding tax.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K17

Cash conversion weakened sharply and financial policy did not adjust: free cash flow fell to USD 168,836 thousand, 31.16% of EBITDA against 73.87% a year earlier, while dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand were 132.61% of it, so cash fell 17.83%. Term-loan repayment slowed to USD 56,264 thousand, and management itself lists cutting dividends among its responses to a cash shortfall, so payouts are the lever that decides whether leverage drifts up.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 75; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K09; calculation K10

Dealer financing is the largest claim outside debt: standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand are 3.79x total debt principal and 2.56x cash plus facility availability, one dealer is 13.0% of net sales, and two floor-plan lenders hold about 50% of floored dollars. Settled repurchase losses have been immaterial and the repurchase price is usually below dealer cost with resale value as an offset, so this is a tail exposure that matters only if a large dealer defaults during a downturn.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K12

Asset quality adds a non-cash risk: goodwill and amortizable intangibles are 37.39% of total assets and about 80% of goodwill sits in reporting units whose fair value exceeds carrying value by less than 25%, so a modest fall in forecasts could force an impairment that cuts equity and reported earnings but not cash, with its covenant treatment not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

Governance risk is medium, not low: no sponsor or controlling holder is identified and audit and reporting quality are high, but the proxy statement, credit agreements and indenture are not supplied and payouts exceeded free cash flow in fiscal 2026, so legal capacity for payouts and guarantor coverage are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

The downside case is a leverage problem, not a liquidity problem: repeating the 37.98% EBITDA decline of the last three years from the fiscal 2026 level gives EBITDA of USD 336,110 thousand and total debt of 2.58x, yet liquidity would still cover a further year of payouts and only small amounts of debt fall due before the facility expires in November 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation K19; calculation K20
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against comfort in the level of credit quality is the trend. Fiscal fourth-quarter EBITDA was 42.17% below the prior year on net sales 8.41% lower, and four times that quarter, USD 520,016 thousand, would already put total debt at 1.67x EBITDA. North American motorized backlog fell 27.5%, and management expects the rest of calendar 2026 and possibly beyond to stay under pressure from interest rates, tariffs and fuel prices linked to disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, so a further decline is plausible rather than remote.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 58; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K05; calculation K18

A stable or rising EBITDA with a margin above 5.64%, while the towable backlog converts and tariff refunds are received, would lift the earnings assessment, and payouts held below free cash flow would remove the policy concern. Total debt above 2.00x EBITDA, which is the analyst's own tripwire and not a covenant, cash plus availability below the January 31, 2026 low of USD 1,240,176 thousand, or a dealer credit event that triggers repurchase demands would move the view down.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 60; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K04; calculation K10
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is calculated from statement lines because no source prints it, so every leverage and coverage conclusion is on a reported, unadjusted basis and a lender definition could move the ratios in either direction.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

- Covenant headroom, guarantor coverage, security and payout capacity cannot be tested because the credit agreements, the indenture and the subsidiary list are not supplied, so structural priority, recovery and legal-capacity conclusions lie outside this view.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 88; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The downside case applies the observed fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026 EBITDA decline to the current year and holds capital spending, interest, working capital and the effective tax rate at fiscal 2026 levels, so its leverage and cash figures are sensitivities and not forecasts.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 67; calculation K19; calculation K20

- No ratings, market prices, peer set or portfolio limits are supplied, so the conclusions on market access and standing against other issuers rest on disclosed fair values and company statements only.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 119; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Fourth-quarter figures are derived as the year less nine months and no balance sheet at October 31, 2025 is supplied, so the 42.17% fourth-quarter EBITDA fall that drives the run-rate conclusion is a calculated figure and not a reported one.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K05
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths

- Low leverage and wide coverage: total debt is 1.60x EBITDA, net debt 0.71x and EBITDA covers cash interest 12.42x, so another weak year can be absorbed before leverage nears any level of concern, which supports the probability of default assessment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K06; calculation K07

- Liquidity and distant maturities: cash of USD 481,988 thousand and about USD 815,000 thousand of facility availability, with 98.09% of principal due in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, leave no refinancing wall before the facility expires in November 2028 and support refinancing capacity.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K10; calculation K11

- Scale and segment diversification: the largest North American maker with a European business and a supply arm kept net sales flat at +0.3% while North American towable sales fell 16.1%, which stabilises revenue and cash generation through a segment downturn.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Debt reduction and creditor-neutral refinancing: term-loan repayments of USD 261,264 thousand over fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026 and margin cuts reduced cash interest paid by 49.51% from fiscal 2024, lowering fixed charges ahead of the earnings decline.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K07; calculation K21

- Reporting quality and no sponsor: unqualified audit opinions, effective internal control and no identified sponsor or controlling holder reduce the risk of misstated figures and of extraction by an owner.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 91; Business & governance (CP-1A)
Weaknesses

- Falling earnings and margin: EBITDA is down 37.98% from fiscal 2023 and EBITDA margin is 5.64%, so operating deleverage turns a modest sales decline into a larger earnings decline and pushes leverage up even as debt falls.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K02; calculation K04; calculation K15

- Payouts above free cash flow: dividends and repurchases of USD 223,891 thousand were 132.61% of free cash flow, so cash fell 17.83% and debt reduction slowed, which makes payout restraint the key policy test.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K09; calculation K10

- Dealer concentration and repurchase obligations: one dealer is 13.0% of net sales and standby repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand are 2.56x cash plus availability, a tail claim that would arrive when liquidity is already tested.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 76; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K12
- Thinly covered goodwill: about 80% of goodwill sits in units with less than 25% headroom, so a forecast cut could trigger an impairment that reduces equity and earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 77; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation K14

- Missing creditor documents and a calculated earnings measure: legal capacity, guarantors and covenant definitions are not established and EBITDA includes gains, so leverage is 1.80x without them, which limits how firmly the level of credit quality can be stated.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 88; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K08
### Company and group structure

Thor is a listed manufacturer with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, so the creditor question is financial policy rather than owner behaviour. It states that it is the sole owner of its operating subsidiaries, which sit in three groups: North American towables and motorized brands, the Erwin Hymer Group in Europe, and the Airxcel and Postle supply businesses, and on July 1, 2026 it took full control of the Roadpass Digital holding company, now under Airxcel. The notes carry guarantees from subsidiaries that are not named in the supplied text, and more than half of cash is held in Europe, so whether the parent and the guarantors can reach the cash and earnings of the European group is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 111; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 112; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk medium: payouts that exceeded free cash flow in one year and missing capacity evidence, against no described liability management, steady debt reduction and maturity extensions with unchanged covenants.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is transactional, discretionary and cyclical rather than recurring: vehicles are built to dealer order, sold to independent dealers who finance inventory with floor-plan lenders, and volume follows consumer confidence and interest rates. In fiscal 2026 shipments fell 11.8% in total and 20.7% in North American towables, while price and mix added 4.6% per unit in towables, so net sales held up through motorized volume, mix and the euro rather than towable demand. Visibility comes from the order backlog, which equals 34.33% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and from one dealer at 13.0% of sales whose bargaining power rises as dealers consolidate.

Pricing power is limited: management chose not to pass on all cost increases including tariff costs in fiscal 2026 to protect dealer and consumer affordability, which keeps revenue in the short term but gives up margin, and sensitivity to interest rates, fuel prices and tariffs is high.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are defended only partly under volume pressure. Material, labour, freight and warranty costs are the main costs, and in North American towables cost of sales rose to 88.8% of net sales from 86.9% as overhead absorption worsened with lower volume, which is why pre-tax income fell 2.51 times as fast as net sales. North American capacity can be cut quickly, but European reductions need works council agreements and bring negotiated separation costs, and restructuring charges rose to USD 58,889 thousand in fiscal 2026 across all segments. Selling, general and administrative expense eased 2.1% mainly through lower incentive pay, a cushion that shrinks as profit falls.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

EBITDA converts weakly into free cash flow in fiscal 2026: 31.16% against 73.87% a year earlier, because operating cash flow fell to USD 321,223 thousand with USD 73,282 thousand absorbed by inventory while capital spending rose to USD 152,387 thousand. Capital spending equals 28.12% of EBITDA and USD 175,000 thousand is committed for fiscal 2027 to be funded from operations; the split between maintenance and growth is not disclosed, so the flexible part is unknown. Cash interest of USD 43,633 thousand is low and falling, and cash taxes of USD 61,802 thousand moved with profit, so the cash cost of debt is not the pressure point; inventory, capital spending and payouts are.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K09; calculation K22
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and entry is easy: about 80 manufacturers compete in the United States and Canada, the principal rivals are Forest River and Winnebago Industries, and the industry has low barriers to entry, so share and price are contested and pricing power is limited. Buyer power is high because one consolidating dealer is 13.0% of sales and two floor-plan lenders decide how much inventory dealers can carry, which can cut orders quickly. Supplier power is concentrated in chassis, where a limited number of suppliers allocate supply in shortages and chassis cannot easily be substituted, and substitutes include used vehicles and other leisure spending, which gain in downturns. Each force acts on volume and margin, not on solvency, and Thor's scale and low leverage let it absorb more of that pressure than a smaller maker.

### Macro and policy factors

Macro and policy factors do alter credit quality here. Tariffs raised component costs that were not fully passed on, a court ruling opened a refund process for tariffs paid under one authority, and a temporary global tariff expired in late July 2026, so net tariff cost is uncertain and refunds could help cash. Interest rates and consumer confidence drive retail demand and dealer carrying costs, fuel prices linked to the Iran conflict may hurt retail demand, emissions rules reach Thor through chassis makers, and new European limits on formaldehyde emissions phase in from calendar 2026 and 2027, which can raise product cost. Currency matters because about 34% of sales are in euros and other currencies and the euro term loan is an economic hedge.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths and weaknesses are ranked above. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the order backlog of USD 3,298,760 thousand converting to sales, possible refunds of tariffs paid, restructuring savings that lift margin, and a European retail market that grew 2.6% in motorcaravans and campervans in the first half of calendar 2026, where Thor gained 7.2%. Threats that could weaken credit quality are a further fall in North American towable retail demand, new tariffs or higher fuel prices, a dealer financing squeeze if floor-plan lenders pull back, chassis shortages, and an impairment of thinly covered goodwill.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The main supports are low leverage, wide coverage, USD 1,296,988 thousand of liquidity and long-dated debt; the constraints are falling and thin margins, weak cash conversion, payouts above free cash flow and contingent dealer claims. The trend is negative on earnings and cash flow and neutral to positive on debt, with total debt falling from USD 1,133,915 thousand in fiscal 2024 to USD 867,959 thousand in fiscal 2026. Access to capital markets is untested in the evidence, but the senior unsecured notes carry a fair value of 93.00% of principal and the term loan 100.43%, so the issuer is not priced as distressed on the issuer's own fair value disclosure. Missing datapoints that would firm up the view are the credit agreements, covenant headroom, guarantor coverage, ratings, market prices, unit-level goodwill headroom and dealer-level repurchase exposure.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the headwinds dominate in North America and the tailwinds sit in Europe and the backlog. The industry association forecasts calendar 2026 North American wholesale shipments of about 314,000 units, 8.2% lower, within a range of 300,000 to 328,100 units, and first-half industry towable retail registrations fell 15.5% while Thor's fell 20.2%, so Thor lost share in towables while dealer inventories fell 12.7% to about 64,000 units and may restock only slowly. In Europe management expects stable volume but pressure on prices and margins, and for the group it plans capital spending of USD 175,000 thousand in fiscal 2027. Over three to five years management remains optimistic about long-term retail demand, a view that is management language and not tested here; the credit event in that window is refinancing the facility in 2028 and USD 859,033 thousand of debt, mostly the notes and the term loan, in fiscal 2030 and fiscal 2031, which low leverage and liquidity make manageable if EBITDA stabilises.

### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is another leg down in North American towable retail demand from high borrowing costs, tariffs and fuel prices, with dealers destocking faster than retail, as in fiscal 2026 when company wholesale units fell 20.5% against retail registrations down 18.5%. The first operational break is operating deleverage in towables, where pre-tax income fell 2.51 times as fast as net sales, and the second is a European margin squeeze. If EBITDA repeated the 37.98% fall of fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2026 from its fiscal 2026 level it would be USD 336,110 thousand, EBITDA margin 3.50%, total debt 2.58x EBITDA and EBITDA 7.70x cash interest; the milder run-rate case of four times the fourth quarter gives USD 520,016 thousand and 1.67x. With capital spending, interest and working capital unchanged and the effective tax rate at 26.8%, free cash flow in the stress case falls to about USD 18,189 thousand, so payouts at the fiscal 2026 level would draw about USD 205,702 thousand of cash and leave about USD 276,286 thousand, while the facility, undrawn at year end, still adds availability subject to its borrowing base, which shrinks with receivables and inventory.

Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 117; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation K15; calculation K18; calculation K19; calculation K20

Management levers are cutting repurchases and dividends, which management lists as responses to a shortfall, reducing capital spending, lowering incentive pay and extending restructuring, and these are enough to avoid a liquidity event in the case shown. The credit event that the levers do not address is a dealer default that triggers repurchase obligations of USD 3,315,731 thousand gross, which is 2.56x liquidity before resale value, and the springing fixed-charge covenant of the facility applies only if excess availability falls below the greater of 10% of the lesser of the borrowing base or facility size and USD 60,000 thousand. Default is not the base case: nothing in the evidence points to one, and liquidity would remain positive in the stress case.
Basis: 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-07-31_tho.htm.jsonl, page 118; calculation K12; calculation K20
### Overall credit view

Overall, Thor presents an adequate business profile supported by North American market leadership, a three-way segment split and a low-leverage balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by three years of falling earnings, payouts above free cash flow and contingent dealer obligations. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but weakening, because free cash flow converted only 31.16% of EBITDA. Reported leverage of 1.60x is low in absolute terms, and no peer set or ratings are supplied for comparison with other leveraged issuers. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA stabilising before the facility expires in November 2028 and the notes fall due in October 2029, with the term loan following in November 2030. The primary downside path is a further fall in North American towable demand that deepens operating deleverage while payouts continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreements, the indenture, the proxy statement, covenant certificates, unit-level goodwill headroom and dealer-level repurchase exposure. Top risk: earnings erosion in North American towables combined with payouts above free cash flow.
